title: Can you audit the coder's negatives at a lower rate and weight them back?
summary: On 3,188 real GoEmotions comments, four automated coders (three cut-offs of a naive-Bayes classifier and a word list; not LLMs) and a hand-coded audit of 100 to 400 items, auditing coder-negative items at a lower rate and weighting them back by stratum size removed the positives-only audit's bias (−0.117 to −0.160, coverage 0.000) but did not narrow the interval. At 200 items the mean 95% width was 0.126 with half the audit among coder-negatives, 0.188 at 20%, 0.259 at 10% and 0.352 at 5%, and the Wald interval under-covered below about 10% (worst-coder coverage 0.85 at 5%, 0.51 at 2%) because only 2–20 negatives were audited. The coder-negative stratum is 69–85% of the corpus and holds 12–16% of it as human positives, so most of the variance is there; the oracle Neyman negative share is 0.63–0.82. The estimated recall was biased upward with few audited negatives. These coders miss 47–65% of positives; a high-recall coder (not tested) might change the answer. One code, one corpus, one split; standard errors ignore the finite-population correction.
lede: can you audit the coder's negatives at a lower rate and weight them back? On 3,188 GoEmotions comments, weighting removes the bias of a positives-only audit but the interval widens as the negative share falls (0.126 at 50%, 0.352 at 5%, 200 items) and under-covers below ~10%. Not an LLM; coders miss half the positives.
